English

[edit]

Adjective

[edit]

pomo

  1. Abbreviation of postmodern.

[edit]
  • For quotations using this term, see Citations:pomo.

Noun

[edit]

pomo (uncountable)

  1. Abbreviation of postmodernism.

[edit]

  • pomophobia
  • pomophobic
  • pomosexual

pomo

Esperanto

[edit]
Esperanto Wikipedia has an article on:
pomo
Wikipedia eo

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French pomme (“apple”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpomo/
  • Audio 1:(file)
  • Audio 2:(file)
  • Rhymes: -omo
  • Syllabification: po‧mo

Noun

[edit]

pomo (accusative singular pomon, plural pomoj, accusative plural pomojn)

  1. apple

Derived terms

[edit]
  • pomarbo (“apple tree”)
  • pomŝteli (“to steal apples, scrump”)
  • pomujo (“basket for collecting apples”)

Finnish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Russian помо́щник (pomóščnik) and shortened.

  • Rhymes: -omo
  • Syllabification(key): po‧mo
  • Hyphenation(key): po‧mo

Noun

[edit]

pomo (colloquial)

  1. boss

Ido

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Esperanto pomo, French pomme, Italian pomo, from Latin pōmum (“fruit”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpɔ.mɔ/, /ˈpo.mo/

Noun

[edit]

pomo (plural pomi)

  1. apple

Derived terms

[edit]
  • pomiero (“apple tree”)
  • pomostumpo (“apple core”)
  • pomosuko (“apple juice”)

Interlingua

[edit]

Noun

[edit]

pomo (plural pomos)

  1. apple

Italian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Latin pōmum (“fruit”), from pōmus, from Proto-Italic *poomos, probably from Proto-Indo-European *h₂po-h₁ém-os (“taken off”), from *h₂epo (“off”) + *h₁em- (“take”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpo.mo/
  • Rhymes: -omo
  • Hyphenation: pó‧mo

Noun

[edit]

pomo m (plural pomi, diminutive pomèllo or (less common) pométto)

  1. knob, pommel
  2. (rare) apple
    Synonym: mela
  3. (by extension) pome, fruit

Related terms

[edit]
  • pometo
  • pomo d'Adamo
  • pomo della discordia
  • pomodoro

Further reading

[edit]
  • pomo in Collins Italian-English Dictionary
  • pomo in Treccani.it – Vocabolario Treccani on line, Istituto dell'Enciclopedia Italiana

Karelian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Ultimately from Russian помо́щник (pomóščnik), possibly shortened from pomoššikka or via Finnish pomo.

Noun

[edit]

pomo (genitive [please provide], partitive [please provide])

  1. boss

References

[edit]

Portuguese

Etymology

[edit]

From Latin pōmum (“fruit”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpõ.mu/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /ˈpõ.mu/

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from Latin pōmum (“fruit”).[1] Cognate with English pome. Also compare English pommel.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /ˈpomo/ [ˈpo.mo]
  • Rhymes: -omo
  • Syllabification: po‧mo

Noun

[edit]

pomo m (plural pomos)

  1. (Spain) knob, doorknob, pommel
    Synonyms: manecilla, perilla
  2. flask (glass bottle)
    Synonym: matraz
  3. fruit tree

Related terms

[edit]
  • poma

References

[edit]
  1. ^ Coromines, Joan; Pascual, José Antonio (1983–1991), “pomo”, in Diccionario crítico etimológico castellano e hispánico [Critical Castilian and Hispanic etymological dictionary]‎[1] (in Spanish), Madrid: Gredos

Further reading

[edit]
  • “pomo”, in Diccionario de la lengua española [Dictionary of the Spanish Language] (in Spanish), online version 23.8.1, Royal Spanish Academy [Spanish: Real Academia Española], 15 December 2025
